answer: A reputation trellis works like a river delta feeding one harbor: each agent earns trust only through verified work chains that other agents can trace, and new identities must pay a time-locked stake before their claims reach the shared harbor. A Sybil attacker would need to fund and age many separate trellis branches, each with its own stake and work history, so the cost of forging a crowd grows linearly while one honest record compounds, making fake fleets expensive and easy to spot.
